definition_zh: 牛仔裤；粗斜纹棉布裤
definition_en: trousers made of strong cotton cloth, usually blue, worn informally by people of any age
core_image: 两条磨得发白的厚棉布裤腿，口袋上钉着黄铜铆钉
scene: 衣柜最下面压着一条穿旧的裤子，膝盖处已经泛白。He pulled on his old jeans and went out to the corner store.
sceneCN: 这里 jeans 是「牛仔裤」（第 1 个义项：粗斜纹棉布做的裤子），句意为他套上旧牛仔裤就去街角小店了。画面里的物件：衣柜、泛白的膝部、门口。

pos.zh: 名词：牛仔裤；粗斜纹布裤（只用复数）

derivatives.zh: 由 jeans 去掉词尾 -s 而来，指牛仔布或牛仔裤单条
同类词，指牛仔布本身，法国布料名 Nîmes 缩合而成
由 jeans 加 -ed 构成，义为「穿着牛仔裤的」，多用于书面描写

senses.title: Trousers of strong cotton cloth
senses.definition: trousers made of a heavy twilled cotton fabric, usually dyed blue
senses.definitionCN: 用厚重的斜纹棉布做成的裤子，通常染成蓝色
senses.example: She bought a pair of jeans with a straight leg.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一条直筒牛仔裤。
senses.why: The word names the cloth before it names the trousers, and the trousers kept the plural shape of the cloth word.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指布料再指裤子，而裤子沿用了布料词的复数外形。

senses.title: A blue-cotton everyday uniform
senses.definition: such trousers worn as tough working clothes rather than as fashion
senses.definitionCN: 指作为耐磨工作服而非时装穿用的这种裤子
senses.example: Miners once wore jeans because the cloth refused to tear.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工当年穿牛仔裤，是因为这种布不容易撕破。
senses.why: The plural word carried the work-clothes sense long before fashion adopted it.
senses.whyCN: 在时装接手之前，这个复数词很久以来一直指工装。

senses.title: A fashion item with a cut or wash
senses.definition: a pair of such trousers treated as a styled garment, described by cut, wash, or finish
senses.definitionCN: 按剪裁、水洗或做旧处理来描述的时装裤装
senses.example: His ripped jeans cost more than my winter coat.
senses.exampleCN: 他那条破洞牛仔裤比我冬天的大衣还贵。
senses.why: Once the garment became a style object, the word picked up the whole vocabulary of cuts and washes.
senses.whyCN: 这条裤子成了时尚对象之后，这个词就带上了整套剪裁与水洗的说法。

senses.title: Denim cloth itself
senses.definition: the twilled cotton fabric from which such trousers are made
senses.definitionCN: 用来做这种裤子的斜纹棉布
senses.example: The jacket is made of dark jeans cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 这件夹克是用深色牛仔布做的。
senses.why: The fabric sense is the older layer of meaning and still survives in compounds.
senses.whyCN: 布料义是这个词更早的一层意思，至今还活在一些复合词里。

senses.title: A casual dress code
senses.definition: an informal standard of dress in which such trousers are acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 允许穿这类裤子的非正式着装标准
senses.example: The office allows jeans on Fridays.
senses.exampleCN: 公司允许周五穿牛仔裤上班。
senses.why: From a garment, the word grew into a label for a whole dress code.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从一件衣服长成了整套着装标准的标签。

intro.en: Jeans is a plural garment word that came into English from the name of a cloth, and the cloth name came from a city.
intro.cn: jeans 是一个复数形式的衣物词，先经由布料名进入英语，而布料名又来自一座城市的名字。

items.en: The cloth name Gene was used in French for a twilled cotton fabric made at Genoa.
items.cn: 法语用 Gene 指热那亚出产的斜纹棉布。

items.en: English borrowed the cloth word as jean or jene in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪把布料词借作 jean 或 jene。

items.en: The plural jeans first named such cloth and later the trousers cut from it.
items.cn: 复数形式 jeans 先指这种布，后来指用它裁成的裤子。

items.en: American workwear of the nineteenth century fixed the blue trousers sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪的美国工装固定了「蓝色长裤」这一义项。

items.en: Denim entered English by another route, from serge de Nîmes.
items.cn: denim 经由另一条路径进入英语，来自「尼姆的哔叽」这一布料名。

note.en: The look-alike group holds cloth and garment words that travel with jeans; the near-meaning group holds other everyday trousers.
note.cn: 形近组收与 jeans 同行的布料和衣物词；近义组收其他日常裤装词。

entries.definition: Heavy twilled cotton used for jeans.
entries.definitionCN: 指做牛仔裤的厚斜纹棉布，与 jeans 常成对出现，但拼写与来源都不同。

entries.definition: The singular form, naming the cloth or one pair.
entries.definitionCN: jeans 的单数形式，指牛仔布或一条裤子。

entries.definition: A general British word for a two-legged garment.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指裤子的英式说法，语法上同样常用复数。

entries.definition: The usual American word for trousers.
entries.definitionCN: 美式英语里最常见的「裤子」。

entries.definition: Smart casual trousers, not denim.
entries.definitionCN: 指较正式的休闲长裤，一般不用牛仔布。

entries.definition: Light cotton trousers in plain colours.
entries.definitionCN: 指素色薄棉布休闲裤。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the city of Genoa to the Friday dress code.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从热那亚这座城走到周五的休闲着装。

normal.en: The cloth name came from Genoa, Italian Genova.
normal.cn: 布料名来自热那亚，意大利语作 Genova。

normal.en: Jeans is normally plural, like trousers and glasses.
normal.cn: jeans 通常用复数，和 trousers、glasses 一样。

normal.en: A pair of jeans is the standard counting pattern.
normal.cn: 计数的标准说法是 a pair of jeans。

normal.en: Denim and jeans are near twins but took different routes.
normal.cn: denim 与 jeans 像双胞胎，但来路不同。

normal.en: Blue jeans fixed the colour sense in American workwear.
normal.cn: 蓝色牛仔裤在美国工装里固定了这个颜色义。

abstract.en: A pair of jeans is a city folded into a pocket.
abstract.cn: 一条牛仔裤就是一座城市折进了口袋。

abstract.en: The rivets are little guarantees that the cloth will hold.
abstract.cn: 铆钉是布料不裂开的小小保证。

abstract.en: Faded knees are a calendar written in cloth.
abstract.cn: 磨白的膝盖是写在布上的日历。

examples.en: These jeans are too tight around the waist.
examples.cn: 这条牛仔裤腰部太紧了。

examples.en: He wears jeans to work on casual days.
examples.cn: 轻松的上班日他穿牛仔裤。

examples.en: The shop sells jeans in every shade of blue.
examples.cn: 这家店卖各种深浅的蓝色牛仔裤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「紧死」—— 牛仔裤穿太紧，就真的紧死了

root: 来自法语布料名 Gene，源于意大利城市 Genoa（热那亚）；十六世纪进入英语作 jean，复数 jeans 后指用它缝制的长裤。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the cotton trousers, their use as work clothes, their life as fashion, the cloth itself, and the dress code they stand for.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：棉布长裤本身、作为工装、作为时装、布料本身，以及它所代表的休闲着装。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thick blue cotton cut into two legs and held by rivets.
core.cn: 核心意象：厚蓝棉布裁成两条裤腿，用铆钉钉牢。

branches.en: THE CLOTH LINE: a fabric that became a pair of trousers.
branches.cn: 布料这条线：一种布变成了裤子。

branches.en: THE MINE LINE: work clothes that refuse to tear.
branches.cn: 矿井这条线：撕不破的工装。

branches.en: THE SHOP WINDOW: cuts, washes, and rips sold as style.
branches.cn: 橱窗这条线：剪裁、水洗、破洞都能卖。

branches.en: THE OFFICE LINE: a garment that marks a whole relaxed day.
branches.cn: 办公室这条线：一件衣服标出整个轻松的日子。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY LINE: tough cloth that also looks personal.
branches.cn: 日常这条线：耐磨的布也能显得有个性。

intro.en: Jeans is borrowed whole, so English adds only endings; the visible endings are the plural -s and the adjective -ed.
intro.cn: jeans 是整体借来的词，英语只添词尾；看得见的是复数 -s 与形容词 -ed。

latinIntro.en: The word comes from a place name rather than a Latin root, so the Latin relatives below are city-name forms only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自地名而非拉丁词根，下面的拉丁条目只是城市名的形式。

items.example: The weaver sold jean by the metre.
The cloth was shipped from Genoa.
It feels like a denimy blue.

items.exampleCN: 蓝色牛仔裤是最常见的。

definition_zh: 珠宝；首饰；珠宝类（总称）
definition_en: rings, necklaces, and other ornaments worn as decoration, taken together as a class of objects
core_image: 绒布上摊开一圈金环、一串珠链和几颗嵌在托里的石头
scene: 柜台的灯打得很亮，托盘里一排镶石头的小饰物闪着光。She keeps her jewellery in a small wooden box.
sceneCN: 这里 jewellery 是「珠宝首饰」（第 1 个义项：作为一类饰物的总称），句意为她把手饰都放在一个小木盒里。画面里的物件：柜台、托盘、木盒。

pos.zh: 名词：珠宝；首饰（不可数的总称）

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，指单颗宝石或一件镶宝石的饰物
由 jewel 加 -er 构成，义为「珠宝商；宝石匠」
由 be- 加 jewel 加 -ed 构成，义为「镶满宝石的」

senses.title: Ornaments worn as a class
senses.definition: rings, necklaces, brooches, and similar ornaments considered together
senses.definitionCN: 戒指、项链、胸针一类饰物合在一起的总称
senses.example: Her jewellery was simple: one ring and a thin chain.
senses.exampleCN: 她的首饰很简单：一枚戒指和一条细链。
senses.why: The word was built as a collective noun, so it names the whole class rather than one item.
senses.whyCN: 这个词天生是集合名词，所以指整类而不是单件。

senses.title: Precious pieces with gems
senses.definition: such ornaments when they hold gold, silver, or cut stones of real value
senses.definitionCN: 指镶有金银或真正宝石、价值较高的饰物
senses.example: The insurance covers the jewellery kept in the safe.
senses.exampleCN: 保险覆盖存放在保险箱里的镶宝首饰。
senses.why: Value is the quality that separates ordinary ornaments from pieces the word most often names.
senses.whyCN: 值钱与否，正是这个词所指对象与普通饰物的分界。

senses.title: The trade and craft
senses.definition: the trade, craft, or industry of making and selling such ornaments
senses.definitionCN: 制作与销售这类饰物的行业或手艺
senses.example: She trained in jewellery before opening her own studio.
senses.exampleCN: 她先学过珠宝工艺，后来才开了自己的工作室。
senses.why: Naming the objects easily slides into naming the business built on them.
senses.whyCN: 指物件很容易就滑向以这些物件为生的行业。

senses.title: Costume ornaments
senses.definition: cheap decorative ornaments made to look like precious ones
senses.definitionCN: 模仿贵重首饰的廉价装饰品
senses.example: The dancers wore bright costume jewellery on stage.
senses.exampleCN: 演员在台上戴着亮闪闪的装饰首饰。
senses.why: Once the word covered all ornaments, cheap imitations could carry it too, usually with a qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词覆盖所有饰物，廉价的仿品也能用它，通常还要加限定词。

senses.title: A personal collection
senses.definition: the set of such ornaments that one person owns and keeps
senses.definitionCN: 某个人拥有并保存的全部这类饰物
senses.example: She left her jewellery to her granddaughter.
senses.exampleCN: 她把首饰留给了孙女。
senses.why: A collective noun naturally comes to mean one household collection.
senses.whyCN: 集合名词很自然地被用来指一户人家的全部收藏。

intro.en: Jewellery is a collective noun built from jewel, and jewel came to English through French from late Latin.
intro.cn: jewellery 是由 jewel 加后缀构成的集合名词，而 jewel 经由法语、从晚期拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: Late Latin jocale meant a plaything or ornament, from jocus, a jest.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 jocale 意为玩物或饰物，源自 jocus「玩笑」。

items.en: Old French turned it into joel or jouel, a precious ornament.
items.cn: 古法语把它变成 joel、jouel，指贵重饰物。

items.en: English borrowed it as jewel and added the agent noun jeweller.
items.cn: 英语借作 jewel，并加 -er 造出 jeweller。

items.en: Jewellery was formed from jeweller as a collective noun in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: jewellery 在十八世纪由 jeweller 派生为集合名词。

items.en: American spelling shortened it to jewelry, while British kept jewellery.
items.cn: 美式拼写简作 jewelry，英式保留 jewellery。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the jewel stem; the near-meaning group holds single ornaments and closely related nouns.
note.cn: 形近组共用 jewel 词干；近义组收单件饰物与关系很近的名词。

entries.definition: A precious stone or one ornament set with one.
entries.definitionCN: 同源基础词，指宝石或单件饰物。

entries.definition: A person who makes or sells jewels.
entries.definitionCN: 由 jewel 加 -er 构成，指珠宝商。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的美式拼写。

entries.definition: A chain or string worn round the neck.
entries.definitionCN: 指项链，是 jewellery 中的一件。

entries.definition: Anything added for decoration.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指装饰品，范围比 jewellery 大得多。

entries.definition: A small cheap ornament.
entries.definitionCN: 指廉价的小饰物，常含轻视意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the Latin plaything to the safe and the insurance list.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「玩物」走到保险箱和保单清单。

normal.en: Late Latin jocale came from jocus, a joke or plaything.
normal.cn: 晚期拉丁语 jocale 源自 jocus，意为玩笑、玩物。

normal.en: English took jewel from French jouel.
normal.cn: 英语从法语 jouel 借来 jewel。

normal.en: Jewellery is uncountable, so a piece of jewellery counts it.
normal.cn: jewellery 不可数，用 a piece of jewellery 来计数。

normal.en: British jewellery doubles the l; American jewelry does not.
normal.cn: 英式 jewellery 双写 l，美式 jewelry 不双写。

normal.en: The same stem gives jeweller and bejewelled.
normal.cn: 同一词干还生出 jeweller 与 bejewelled。

abstract.en: Jewellery is a family of small lights kept in one box.
abstract.cn: 首饰是一盒收在一起的许多小光点。

abstract.en: A jewel is one star; jewellery is the whole night sky.
abstract.cn: jewel 是一颗星，jewellery 是整片夜空。

abstract.en: The old word for a plaything became the word for treasure.
abstract.cn: 曾经的「玩物」一词变成了「珍宝」一词。

examples.en: She never travels with her jewellery.
examples.cn: 她从不带着首饰出门。

examples.en: The museum displays jewellery from ancient tombs.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出古墓出土的首饰。

examples.en: Cheap jewellery can still look elegant.
examples.cn: 廉价的首饰也能显得雅致。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「久饿而绿」—— 首饰放久了不戴，铜的都会变绿

root: 晚期拉丁语 jocale「玩物、饰物」（源自 jocus「玩笑」）→ 古法语 joel、jouel → 英语 jewel → 加 -ery 构成集合名词 jewellery。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the class of ornaments, precious pieces, the trade, cheap imitations, and the collection of one person.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：饰物总称、镶宝首饰、珠宝行业、装饰仿品，以及个人的全部珍藏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small bright objects spread on dark velvet.
core.cn: 核心意象：深色绒布上摊开的小而亮的东西。

branches.en: THE DISH LINE: rings and chains lying together as one group.
branches.cn: 托盘这条线：戒指和链子一起摊成一组。

branches.en: THE SAFE LINE: stones valuable enough to be insured.
branches.cn: 保险箱这条线：值钱到需要上保险的石头。

branches.en: THE WORKSHOP: the craft that turns stones into a living.
branches.cn: 工坊这条线：把手艺变成生计。

branches.en: THE STAGE: bright imitations worn under the lights.
branches.cn: 舞台这条线：灯光下戴着的亮仿品。

branches.en: THE BOX LINE: what one woman keeps and passes on.
branches.cn: 木盒这条线：一个人收藏并传下去的东西。

intro.en: Jewellery is jewel plus a collective ending; English endings do the visible work here.
intro.cn: jewellery 是 jewel 加集合后缀，这里起作用的主要是英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The deeper relatives descend from late Latin jocale, a plaything.
latinIntro.cn: 更深的同族可追到晚期拉丁语 jocale「玩物」。

items.example: The jewel fell from its setting.
items.exampleCN: 那颗石子从托上掉了下来。
它把 jeweller 变成 jewellery。
英式拼写保留了两个 l。
它把词变成形容词 bejewelled。

items.example: A jewelly shine is a loose description.
items.exampleCN: 有光泽像珠宝是一种随意的描写。

definition_zh: 工作；职业；任务；活儿；职位
definition_en: the paid work that someone does regularly, or one particular task that has to be done
core_image: 一张排满格子的日程表，每格都写着待办的事
scene: 面试结束后，她站在走廊里等电梯，手里还捏着简历。She spent three months looking for a job in the city.
sceneCN: 这里 job 是「工作、职业」（第 1 个义项：为取得报酬而长期做的事），句意为她在这座城市找工作找了三个月。画面里的物件：走廊、电梯、简历。

pos.zh: 名词：工作；职业；职位；任务；活儿
动词：打零工（口语）

derivatives.zh: 由 job 加 -less 构成，义为「失业的」
由 job 加 -ing 构成，义为「打零工的；做零活的」
由 job 加 -er 构成，指散户经纪或做零活的人

senses.title: Paid work done regularly
senses.definition: the regular paid work that a person does to earn a living
senses.definitionCN: 一个人为谋生而长期从事的有偿工作
senses.example: She found a job in a bookshop near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她在车站附近的书店找到了一份工作。
senses.why: The core sense is regular paid work, the thing a person most often asks another about.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是长期有偿工作，也就是人们最常问起的那件事。

senses.title: A position in a firm
senses.definition: a particular post or opening that someone can be hired to fill
senses.definitionCN: 某个可以被雇用填补的具体岗位
senses.example: Fifty people applied for the job.
senses.exampleCN: 有五十人申请这个岗位。
senses.why: A job can be seen as a slot to be filled, separate from the person filling it.
senses.whyCN: job 也能被看作一个待填的位置，与填它的人分开。

senses.title: A single task
senses.definition: one particular piece of work that must be finished
senses.definitionCN: 一件必须完成的特定工作
senses.example: Cleaning the gutters is a nasty job.
senses.exampleCN: 清理屋檐水槽是件麻烦的任务。
senses.why: The countable task sense narrows regular work down to one piece of it.
senses.whyCN: 可数的任务义把长期工作缩成其中的一件。

senses.title: Quality of work done
senses.definition: the standard or quality of a piece of work, as in doing a good job
senses.definitionCN: 某项工作的水准，如「干得好」
senses.example: You did a good job on that report.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告你写得不错。
senses.why: Judging how a job was done blends the task sense with an evaluation.
senses.whyCN: 评价活儿干得怎么样，是任务义与评价的融合。

senses.title: A fixed duty or role
senses.definition: something treated as a duty that belongs to a person
senses.definitionCN: 被视为某人分内应做的事
senses.example: It is not my job to answer the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 接电话不是我的职责。
senses.why: When a duty is assigned, the word slides from the work to the person expected to do it.
senses.whyCN: 当职责被指派时，这个词就从工作滑到了该做工作的人身上。

senses.title: To work by the piece
senses.definition: to do small or piece-rate work, often casually
senses.definitionCN: 做零散或计件的工作，多为临时性质
senses.example: He jobbed on building sites for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 他在工地打了一年零工。
senses.why: The verb keeps only the piecework shadow of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词只保留了名词「零活」的那道影子。

intro.en: Job is a word of uncertain origin; the usual view links it to a lump or piece of work, but the earlier steps are disputed.
intro.cn: job 的来源一般认为不确定；常见看法把它连到「一块、一桩」的活儿，但更早的脉络尚有争议。

items.en: The word appears in English in the sixteenth century with the sense of a piece of work.
items.cn: 这个词十六世纪出现于英语，义为「一桩活儿」。

items.en: Some scholars connect it with gob, a lump or mass, meaning a lump of work.
items.cn: 一些学者把它连到 gob「一块、一团」，意为一团活儿。

items.en: Others treat it as unrelated slang of unknown source.
items.cn: 另一些人认为它是来源不明的俚语，与此无关。

items.en: By the seventeenth century it meant regular paid employment.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，它已指长期的有偿雇用。

items.en: The verb and the phrases do a good job spread in the modern period.
items.cn: 动词用法与 do a good job 一类说法在近现代铺开。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words that are easy to confuse with job; the near-meaning group holds other words for work and tasks.
note.cn: 形近组收容易与 job 混看的短词；近义组收表示工作与任务的其他词。

entries.definition: To run slowly and steadily.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写只差一个字母，义为「慢跑」，来源不同。

entries.definition: To write something down quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，义为「匆匆记下」，来源不同。

entries.definition: A shrub grown for its oil.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近的植物名，来源完全不同。

entries.definition: Activity done to achieve a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 不可数的「工作」，范围比 job 宽。

entries.definition: The whole course of a working life.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个职业生涯，比 job 长。

entries.definition: One piece of work to be done.
entries.definitionCN: 指一项具体任务，与第 3 个义项最近。

entries.definition: A particular position of employment.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式的「职位」，与第 2 个义项相近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a lump of work to a slot in the job market.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从「一团活儿」走到就业市场里的一个空位。

normal.en: Job is countable, so we say a job and two jobs.
normal.cn: job 可数，说 a job、two jobs。

normal.en: Work is usually uncountable, which is the classic contrast.
normal.cn: work 通常不可数，这是最经典的对比。

normal.en: A job interview is where a person meets a post.
normal.cn: job interview 是人去会一个岗位的场合。

normal.en: Do a good job judges the task, not the post.
normal.cn: do a good job 评的是活儿，不是岗位。

normal.en: Jobless adds -less to turn the noun into an adjective.
normal.cn: jobless 加 -less 把名词变成形容词。

abstract.en: A job is a box on a timetable that someone pays to fill.
abstract.cn: 工作是日程表上有人付钱让人填的一格。

abstract.en: The same word covers a life and an afternoon.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指一辈子也指一个下午。

abstract.en: Every task is a small job inside a big one.
abstract.cn: 每项任务都是大活儿里的小活儿。

examples.en: He took a job at a small factory.
examples.cn: 他在一家小厂找了份工作。

examples.en: Finishing the roof was a two-day job.
examples.cn: 修完屋顶是两天的活儿。

examples.en: She did a fine job of explaining the rules.
examples.cn: 她把规则解释得很清楚。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: regular paid work, a post, one task, the quality of work, a fixed duty, and the verb for piecework.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：长期有偿工作、岗位、单项任务、活儿的质量、分内职责，以及打零工的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a filled square on a timetable, each square paid for.
core.cn: 核心意象：日程表上一格一格被填满、并且有人付钱的方块。

branches.en: THE DESK LINE: work that repeats every weekday.
branches.cn: 办公桌这条线：每个工作日重复的工作。

branches.en: THE NOTICE BOARD: an opening that many people want.
branches.cn: 公告栏这条线：许多人争的一个空位。

branches.en: THE CHORE LINE: one task and how well it was done.
branches.cn: 杂活这条线：一项任务以及干得好不好。

branches.en: THE ROTA: the duty that belongs to a name.
branches.cn: 值班表这条线：写着一个名字的职责。

branches.en: THE SITE LINE: casual work paid by the piece.
branches.cn: 工地这条线：按件付钱的零活。

intro.en: Job is a short native-style word; English builds its family with endings rather than a Latin stem.
intro.cn: job 是很短的英语词，词族靠英语词尾扩展，没有拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root behind job, so the list below stays empty.

definition_zh: 加入；连接；参加；把……接起来；会合
definition_en: to become a member of a group, or to fasten two or more things together so that they touch or form one thing
core_image: 两块木料被一道榫头咬合在一起，接缝看不出来
scene: 社团招新的长桌摆在广场中央，路过的人停下填表。Over a hundred students joined the club in its first week.
sceneCN: 这里 join 是「加入」（第 1 个义项：成为某个团体的成员），句意为社团成立第一周就有一百多名学生加入。画面里的物件：长桌、表格、广场。

pos.zh: 动词：加入；参加；连接；会合

derivatives.zh: 由 join 加 -t 构成，指接合处或关节
由 joint 加 -ly 构成，义为「共同地、连带地」
由 join 加 -er 构成，义为「细木工匠」
由 join 加 -ing 构成，义为「连接；接合处」
加 en- 前缀构成，义为「责令；禁止」

senses.title: To become a member
senses.definition: to become a member of a group, club, company, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 成为某个团体、社团、公司或组织的成员
senses.example: She joined the debating society in her first term.
senses.exampleCN: 她在第一个学期加入了辩论社。
senses.why: Membership is a joining of oneself to a body, the same act as joining two things.
senses.whyCN: 加入就是把自己接到一个群体上，与把两样东西接起来是同一个动作。

senses.title: To fasten things together
senses.definition: to fasten two or more things so that they are linked or become one
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或多个东西接在一起，使其相连或成为一体
senses.example: Join the two pipes with a short metal collar.
senses.exampleCN: 用一段短金属箍把两根管子接起来。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical layer: two edges brought to touch.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的物理层含义：两条边被凑到一起。

senses.title: To take part in an activity
senses.definition: to take part in something that others are already doing
senses.definitionCN: 参与别人已经在做的事
senses.example: Do come and join the game after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后一定来参加游戏。
senses.why: Taking part is joining one activity rather than one organization.
senses.whyCN: 参加指的是加入一项活动，而不是一个组织。

senses.title: To meet and merge
senses.definition: to meet and combine, as roads, rivers, or people on a route
senses.definitionCN: 指道路、河流或路上的人在一点汇合
senses.example: The two paths join just below the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 两条小路就在桥下会合。
senses.why: Two lines meeting is the physical joining seen from the path itself.
senses.whyCN: 两条线交汇，就是站在路的角度看的「接合」。

senses.title: To share in a feeling or action
senses.definition: to share an action or feeling with someone, often in a set phrase
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法中与他人共同做某事或共有某种感受
senses.example: The whole hall joined in the chorus.
senses.exampleCN: 全场一起唱起了副歌。
senses.why: Joining a voice to others extends the fastener image to sound and feeling.
senses.whyCN: 把自己的声音接到别人那里，是把接合的画面延伸到声音与情绪上。

intro.en: Join comes from French joindre, from Latin jungere, "to yoke or connect"; the same root gives junction and jugular.
intro.cn: join 来自法语 joindre，源于拉丁语 jungere「套轭、连接」；同一词根还生出 junction、jugular。

items.en: jungere meant to join or yoke animals together, from jugum, a yoke.
items.cn: jungere 意为把牲口套在一起，源自 jugum「轭」。

items.en: junctus was its past participle, giving the stem junct- seen in junction.
items.cn: 过去分词 junctus 给出 junct- 词干，见于 junction。

items.en: Old French joindre softened the consonant and dropped the nasal ending in speech.
items.cn: 古法语 joindre 软化了辅音，口语里还丢了鼻音词尾。

items.en: English borrowed join in the thirteenth century for both uniting and becoming a member.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 join，既指连接也指成为成员。

items.en: Join up and join in fixed the phrasal uses in later centuries.
items.cn: join up 与 join in 在后几个世纪固定为短语动词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin jung- stem; the near-meaning group holds verbs for connecting and taking part.
note.cn: 形近组共用拉丁词干 jung-；近义组收表示连接与参与的词。

entries.definition: A place where two parts are connected.
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，指接合处或关节。

entries.definition: A point where things meet, especially roads.
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，指交汇处，尤指路口。

entries.definition: A craftsman who makes wooden joints.
entries.definitionCN: 由 join 加 -er 构成，指细木工匠。

entries.definition: To link two things together.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「连接」，语气更中性。

entries.definition: To go into a place or group.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「进入」，强调走进去。

entries.definition: To register as a member of a course.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指注册入学或入会。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from the Latin yoke to the club table on the square.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「轭」走到广场上的招新长桌。

normal.en: Latin jungere meant to yoke animals together.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jungere 意为把牲口套在一起。

normal.en: The same root gives joint, junction, and juncture.
normal.cn: 同一词根生出 joint、junction、juncture。

normal.en: Join a club takes a direct object with no preposition.
normal.cn: join a club 直接跟宾语，不加介词。

normal.en: Join in is used for activities rather than organizations.
normal.cn: join in 用于活动，而不是组织。

normal.en: Join forces means two sides put their strength together.
normal.cn: join forces 指双方把力量合在一起。

abstract.en: To join is to put two edges so close the seam disappears.
abstract.cn: 加入就是把两条边贴到接缝合拢。

abstract.en: A yoke over two necks is the oldest picture of the word.
abstract.cn: 横在两条脖子上的轭，是这个词最老的画面。

abstract.en: Every member is one more thread tied to the same rope.
abstract.cn: 每个成员都是系在同一根绳上的又一根线。

examples.en: He joined the company as a junior clerk.
examples.cn: 他作为初级职员加入了这家公司。

examples.en: Join the two wires and wrap them with tape.
examples.cn: 把两根线接上，再用胶布缠好。

examples.en: Will you join us for lunch?
examples.cn: 你跟我们一起去吃午饭吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佐因」—— 佐理的人进来，就是加入

root: 拉丁语 jungere「套轭、连接」（源自 jugum「轭」）→ 过去分词 junctus → 古法语 joindre → 英语 join。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: becoming a member, fastening things, taking part, meeting and merging, and sharing in an action.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：成为成员、把东西接起来、参加活动、会合，以及一同参与。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two edges brought together until the seam cannot be seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条边被凑到一起，直到看不见接缝。

branches.en: THE CLUB TABLE: a name written on a list of members.
branches.cn: 招新桌这条线：名字写进会员名单。

branches.en: THE PIPE LINE: two ends fitted into one collar.
branches.cn: 管子这条线：两个端头套进同一个箍。

branches.en: THE GAME LINE: stepping in while others already play.
branches.cn: 游戏这条线：别人已经在玩时走进去。

branches.en: THE CROSSROADS: two paths becoming one below the bridge.
branches.cn: 路口这条线：两条路在桥下合成一条。

branches.en: THE CHORUS: one voice added to many.
branches.cn: 合唱这条线：一个声音加进许多声音。

intro.en: Join carries the Latin stem jung- and takes English endings for its family.
intro.cn: join 带着拉丁词干 jung-，其词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives all descend from jungere, to yoke.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词都源自 jungere「套轭」。

items.meaning: to connect or become a member
items.example: They join the parts by hand.
items.exampleCN: 他们手工把零件接起来。

definition_zh: 共同地；连带地；联合地
definition_en: in a way shared by two or more people or groups, who act or are responsible together
core_image: 两只手握在同一支笔上，一起在同一张纸上签名
scene: 两家公司各派一名代表坐在长桌两侧，同时签字。The flat is owned jointly by the two sisters.
sceneCN: 这里 jointly 是「共同地」（第 1 个义项：由两个或更多方一起做或共有），句意为这套房子由姐妹俩共同拥有。画面里的物件：长桌、代表、签字笔。

pos.zh: 副词：共同地；连带地；联合地

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「联合的；共同的」
基础词名词义，指接合处或关节
joint 与 jointly 的动词来源，义为「连接；加入」

senses.title: Shared by more than one party
senses.definition: in a way that is shared by two or more people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 由两个或更多人或团体共同分享的方式
senses.example: The two families jointly own the orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 两个家庭共同拥有这片果园。
senses.why: Jointly marks the sharing of one thing by more than one side.
senses.whyCN: jointly 标出一样东西被不止一方分享。

senses.title: Acting together
senses.definition: by acting together rather than separately
senses.definitionCN: 指一起行动而不是各自行动
senses.example: The police and the council acted jointly on the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 警方和议会在该方案上联合行动。
senses.why: From sharing an object the word moves to sharing an action.
senses.whyCN: 从共有一个东西，这个词转向共做一个动作。

senses.title: Legally liable together
senses.definition: in law, so that the parties share a single liability or right
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指各方共同承担同一份责任或权利
senses.example: They signed jointly and severally for the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为这笔贷款签了连带责任。
senses.why: The legal sense fixes joint liability in one adverb.
senses.whyCN: 法律义用一个副词把连带责任固定下来。

senses.title: Written or produced by two authors
senses.definition: with two or more named authors or makers
senses.definitionCN: 指由两位或更多署名作者共同写出或制作
senses.example: The paper was written jointly by a chemist and a historian.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文由一位化学家和一位历史学家合写。
senses.why: Authorship is another kind of sharing that the adverb labels.
senses.whyCN: 署名是另一种共同分享，这个副词同样能标注。

senses.title: Together in a single arrangement
senses.definition: considered together as one arrangement rather than in parts
senses.definitionCN: 指把几样东西作为一个整体来合计
senses.example: The units are jointly managed by one committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这些单位由同一个委员会共同管理。
senses.why: Managing several things as one unit is the same sharing seen from the institution side.
senses.whyCN: 把几样东西当一个单位来管，是同一份共享从机构角度看的样子。

intro.en: Jointly is joint plus the adverb ending -ly; joint itself comes from Latin junctus through French.
intro.cn: jointly 是 joint 加副词词尾 -ly；joint 本身经由法语来自拉丁语 junctus。

items.en: junctus, the past participle of jungere, meant joined.
items.cn: jungere 的过去分词 junctus 意为「被连接的」。

items.en: Old French joint named a joining or a place where two parts meet.
items.cn: 古法语 joint 指接合，或两部分的相接处。

items.en: English took joint as noun and adjective, meaning a place of meeting and then shared.
items.cn: 英语把 joint 用作名词和形容词，先指相接处，后指共同的。

items.en: The adverb jointly formed with -ly to mark shared action.
items.cn: 副词 jointly 由 -ly 构成，用来标记共同的行为。

items.en: Legal usage fixed the pair jointly and severally.
items.cn: 法律用法固定了 jointly and severally 这一对说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the join stem; the near-meaning group holds adverbs and phrases for shared action.
note.cn: 形近组共用 join 词干；近义组收表示共同行动的副词与说法。

entries.definition: Shared, or a place where parts meet.
entries.definitionCN: 同源的基础形容词，义为「共同的」或指接合处。

entries.definition: Having joints, as a doll or stem.
entries.definitionCN: 由 joint 加 -ed 构成，义为「有关节的」。

entries.definition: To connect or become a member.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「连接；加入」。

entries.definition: With each other, in one place or group.
entries.definitionCN: 副词义为「一起」，最口语。

entries.definition: As a whole group rather than separately.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，强调作为整体。

entries.definition: In a way felt or done by both sides.
entries.definitionCN: 强调双方互相的。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from the Latin participle to a lease with two signatures.

normal.cn: jointly 就是 joint 加副词词尾 -ly。

normal.cn: joint 来自拉丁语 junctus「被连接的」。

normal.en: Jointly owned and jointly responsible are the common pairs.
normal.cn: jointly owned 与 jointly responsible 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: In law, jointly and severally means shared and separate liability.
normal.cn: 法律上 jointly and severally 指连带责任。

normal.en: The word always needs at least two parties.
normal.cn: 这个词永远需要至少两方。

abstract.en: Two hands on one pen is the picture of jointly.
abstract.cn: 两只手握着同一支笔，就是 jointly 的画面。

abstract.en: Sharing an object, then a duty, then a signature.
abstract.cn: 先共有一个东西，再共有职责，再共有签名。

abstract.en: Jointly is the seam where two lives write one line.
abstract.cn: 共同就是把两条人生缝成一行字的地方。

examples.en: The land is jointly owned by the two villages.
examples.cn: 这块地由这两个村子共有。

examples.en: The report was jointly produced by three agencies.
examples.cn: 这份报告由三个机构联合完成。

examples.en: They are jointly responsible for the repairs.
examples.cn: 他们对维修共同负责。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「找因特里」—— 两家人一起找原因，就是共同地

branches.cn: 地契这条线：一块地写着两个名字。

branches.cn: 行动这条线：两个机构同时出手。

branches.en: THE CONTRACT: one debt hanging over two shoulders.
branches.cn: 合同这条线：一笔债压在两个肩膀上。

branches.en: THE TITLE PAGE: two names under one heading.
branches.cn: 标题页这条线：一个标题下两个署名。

branches.cn: 委员会这条线：若干单位由一张桌子管。

items.example: Jointly and severally is a legal pair.
items.exampleCN: jointly 与 severally 是法律上的配对。

definition_zh: 笑话；玩笑；笑料；开玩笑道；开玩笑的对象
definition_en: something said or done to make people laugh, or a person or thing that invites teasing
core_image: 一桌人听到一句话后同时笑出声，杯子都晃了一下
scene: 晚饭后客厅里坐满亲戚，舅舅讲起年轻时的糗事。His story about the broken chair got the biggest joke of the evening.
sceneCN: 这里 joke 是「笑话」（第 1 个义项：引人发笑的话或事），句意为他把那把坏椅子的糗事讲得成了当晚最大的笑料。画面里的物件：客厅、沙发、茶杯。

pos.zh: 名词：笑话；玩笑；笑料；笑柄
动词：开玩笑；说笑话

derivatives.zh: 由 joke 加 -er 构成，义为「爱开玩笑的人；扑克里的大王」
由 joke 加 -ing 构成，义为「开玩笑的」
由 joking 加 -ly 构成，义为「开玩笑地」
由 joke 加 -y 构成，义为「爱打趣的；轻松逗趣的」

senses.title: Something said to make people laugh
senses.definition: a short story or remark with a funny turn that makes people laugh
senses.definitionCN: 带有出人意料的滑稽转折，使人发笑的话或短故事
senses.example: He told a joke about two penguins on a bus.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲了个关于两只企鹅坐公交的笑话。
senses.why: The core sense is a spoken turn that produces laughter.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一个说出后引来笑声的转折。

senses.title: A playful act or trick
senses.definition: a playful act, often at somebody else's expense
senses.definitionCN: 一种戏耍的举动，常以别人为对象
senses.example: Hiding his shoes was meant as a joke.
senses.exampleCN: 把他的鞋藏起来原本是开玩笑。
senses.why: The word widens from a spoken thing to a done thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从说出来的东西扩大到做出来的东西。

senses.title: A mocking remark
senses.definition: a remark made lightly to tease or mock someone
senses.definitionCN: 轻描淡写地用来取笑或挖苦某人的话
senses.example: The boys made jokes about his new haircut.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩们拿他的新发型说笑。
senses.why: Laughter can be turned on a person, and the same noun follows.
senses.whyCN: 笑声可以转向某个人，同一个名词也跟着转。

senses.title: A person or thing that invites teasing
senses.definition: a person, plan, or object that seems ridiculous to others
senses.definitionCN: 被别人看作可笑的人、计划或东西
senses.example: The new rule became the joke of the whole office.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定成了整个办公室的笑柄。
senses.why: When the funny thing is the target itself, the noun becomes a label for it.
senses.whyCN: 当可笑的对象本身就是目标时，这个名词就变成给它的标签。

senses.title: To speak or act playfully
senses.definition: to say or do something in play, expecting no serious answer
senses.definitionCN: 带着玩闹意味说话或行事，不指望当真回应
senses.example: I was only joking about the price.
senses.exampleCN: 我不过是拿价格开玩笑。
senses.why: The verb keeps the light, half-serious tone of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了名词那半真半假、轻松的语气。

senses.title: Hard to take seriously
senses.definition: used to say that something is so easy or small it is not worth calling a task
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示某事太容易、太微小，不值得称作难题
senses.example: Fixing that is no joke for a beginner.
senses.exampleCN: 对新手来说，修好那东西可不是说说而已。
senses.why: The idiomatic use keeps the word for things that look light but turn heavy.
senses.whyCN: 这个习语义保留了对「看着轻、其实重」的事物使用该词。

intro.en: Joke came from Latin jocus, a jest, through Italian and French before it reached English.
intro.cn: joke 源于拉丁语 jocus「玩笑」，经由意大利语和法语才进入英语。

items.en: jocus meant a jest, a joke, or a playful word.
items.cn: jocus 意为玩笑、笑话或打趣的话。

items.en: Italian gioco carried the sense of play or sport.
items.cn: 意大利语 gioco 带着「游戏、玩」的意思。

items.en: French jocque named a light saying, and English met the word there.
items.cn: 法语 jocque 指轻松的话，英语是在这里遇到这个词的。

items.en: Joke entered English in the seventeenth century as a noun.
items.cn: joke 在十七世纪作为名词进入英语。

items.en: The verb and the phrase no joke followed within a century.
items.cn: 动词用法与 no joke 的说法在一个世纪内跟上。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the joke family; the near-meaning group holds other kinds of fun and laughter.
note.cn: 形近组共用 joke 这一族词；近义组收其他表示玩笑与好笑事物的词。

entries.definition: Someone who jokes, or the highest card in a pack.
entries.definitionCN: 由 joke 加 -er 构成，指爱开玩笑的人或扑克大王。

entries.definition: In a joking manner.
entries.definitionCN: 由 joke 派生，义为「开玩笑地」。

entries.definition: Formal word for playful and humorous.
entries.definitionCN: 同源于拉丁 jocus，较正式的「诙谐的」。

entries.definition: A joke, often in older writing.
entries.definitionCN: 较文雅的说法，义为「玩笑」，多见于旧文字。

entries.definition: A practical joke played on someone.
entries.definitionCN: 指针对某人的恶作剧。

entries.definition: A short joke, often written for a performer.
entries.definitionCN: 口语里指短小的笑话段子。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the Latin jest to the phrase no joke.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「玩笑」走到 no joke 这种说法。

normal.en: Latin jocus is also the source of jocose.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jocus 也是 jocose 的来源。

normal.en: Tell a joke is the standard verb pair.
normal.cn: tell a joke 是最标准的动词搭配。

normal.en: Play a joke on someone means the target is a person.
normal.cn: play a joke on someone 指被开玩笑的是人。

normal.en: A practical joke is done rather than told.
normal.cn: practical joke 是做出来的，不是讲出来的。

normal.en: No joke means something is serious after all.
normal.cn: no joke 表示某事其实很严重。

abstract.en: A joke is a small trap set for laughter.
abstract.cn: 笑话是给笑声设的小陷阱。

abstract.en: The same word can be the laughter and the one laughed at.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可以是笑声，也可以是被笑的人。

abstract.en: A joke dies the moment it is explained.
abstract.cn: 笑话一解释就死了。

examples.en: She told a joke that made everyone laugh.
examples.cn: 她讲了个让大家发笑的笑话。

examples.en: They joked about the endless rain all week.
examples.cn: 他们整周都拿下不完的雨开玩笑。

examples.en: Nobody could take his excuse as a joke.
examples.cn: 没人能把他的借口当成玩笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「揍客」—— 玩笑开过头，客人就想揍人

root: 拉丁语 jocus「玩笑、戏谑」→ 意大利语 gioco → 法语 jocque → 英语 joke；同族还有 jocose、jocular。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: a funny story, a playful act, a mocking remark, the laughing stock, the verb, and the ironic phrase no joke.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：笑话、玩笑举动、取笑的话、笑柄、开玩笑的动词义，以及 no joke 这一反讽说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoken turn that ends in a room full of laughter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话的转折让满屋子人笑出声。

branches.en: THE DINNER TABLE: a story with a funny ending.
branches.cn: 餐桌这条线：有滑稽结尾的故事。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN SHOES: a trick done rather than told.
branches.cn: 藏起的鞋这条线：做出来而不是讲出来的玩笑。

branches.en: THE SCHOOLYARD: laughter aimed at a person.
branches.cn: 校园这条线：笑声对准了某个人。

branches.en: THE NOTICE BOARD: a rule that everyone ridicules.
branches.cn: 公告板这条线：被所有人嘲笑的规定。

branches.en: THE HALF-SERIOUS VOICE: the joking verb and the phrase about weight.
branches.cn: 半真半假的口气：开玩笑的动词义与表示分量的说法。

intro.en: Joke takes only English endings; the Latin joc- stem shows up in its formal cousins.
intro.cn: joke 只加英语词尾，拉丁 joc- 词干出现在它较正式的亲属词里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives descend from jocus, a jest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词源自 jocus「玩笑」。

items.exampleCN: no joke 意为非同小可。

definition_zh: 日报；杂志；期刊；日志；日记
definition_en: a magazine or newspaper on a serious subject, or a daily written record of what happens
core_image: 一叠按日期装订起来、纸边写满小字的册子
scene: 图书馆的报刊区，一排放着硬壳合订本，书脊上印着年份。She published her first paper in a medical journal last spring.
sceneCN: 这里 journal 是「期刊」（第 1 个义项：定期出版的专门刊物），句意为她去年春天在医学期刊上发表了第一篇论文。画面里的物件：图书馆、合订本、书脊。

pos.zh: 名词：期刊；杂志；日志；日记

derivatives.zh: 由 journal 加 -ist 构成，义为「新闻工作者」
由 journalist 加 -ism 构成，义为「新闻业；新闻学」
由 journalist 加 -ic 构成，义为「新闻业的」
由 journal 加 -ed 构成，义为「记入日志的」（英式双写 l）

senses.title: A periodical on a special subject
senses.definition: a periodical, often containing serious articles, published for a profession or field
senses.definitionCN: 为某一行业或领域出版的定期刊物，多载严肃文章
senses.example: Her study appeared in a well-known journal.
senses.exampleCN: 她的研究发表在一份知名期刊上。
senses.why: The periodical sense grew out of the idea of something issued day by day.
senses.whyCN: 期刊义是从「按日发行」这个概念长出来的。

senses.title: A daily newspaper
senses.definition: a newspaper published every day, now mostly in formal or older usage
senses.definitionCN: 每天出版的报纸，现在多用于正式或较早的语境
senses.example: The news was read aloud from the local journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这条消息是从当地日报上念出来的。
senses.why: A newspaper issued every day takes its name straight from the daily book.
senses.whyCN: 日报每天发行，名字直接来自「每日的簿册」。

senses.title: A personal daily record
senses.definition: a book in which a person writes down events and thoughts each day
senses.definitionCN: 每天记下事情与想法的本子
senses.example: She has kept a journal since she was ten.
senses.exampleCN: 她十岁起就记日记。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is a book kept day by day by one person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层，是一个人按天记下的本子。

senses.title: A log of an activity
senses.definition: an official record of what is done, as in a ship or a laboratory
senses.definitionCN: 对所做之事的正式记录，如船上或实验室的记录
senses.example: The engineer noted the fault in the engine journal.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把这个故障记在了轮机日志里。
senses.why: A ship or a lab keeps the same day book, but for duty rather than feeling.
senses.whyCN: 船上或实验室也记同样的日簿，只是记的是职责而不是心情。

senses.title: A published volume of papers
senses.definition: a volume collecting the proceedings or papers of a learned society
senses.definitionCN: 汇集某学会会议记录或论文的册子
senses.example: The society prints its journal every quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 该学会每季度印行自己的汇编。
senses.why: Issuing papers at fixed dates turns a day book into a journal for a whole field.
senses.whyCN: 按固定日期印行论文，把日簿变成面向整个领域的期刊。

senses.title: A travel account
senses.definition: a written account of travels, usually kept day by day
senses.definitionCN: 通常按天记录下来的行旅文字
senses.example: His travel journal became a small book.
senses.exampleCN: 他的旅行日志后来成了一本小书。
senses.why: Travellers keep the same daily habit, so the word follows them on the road.
senses.whyCN: 旅人保留同样的按天记录习惯，这个词就跟着他们上路。

intro.en: Journal comes from French journal, a daily book, which descends from Latin diurnalis, "of the day".
intro.cn: journal 来自法语 journal「每日的书」，其源头是拉丁语 diurnalis「每日的」。

items.en: diurnus meant of the day, from dies, a day.
items.cn: diurnus 意为「白日的」，源自 dies「日」。

items.en: diurnalis was the adjective built on diurnus.
items.cn: diurnalis 是由 diurnus 构成的形容词。

items.en: Old French journal meant daily, and also a daily record or book.
items.cn: 古法语 journal 既指「每日的」，也指每日的记录或簿册。

items.en: English adopted journal for a daily account and later for a newspaper.
items.cn: 英语借入 journal 指每日记述，后来又指报纸。

items.en: The learned periodical sense became dominant in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 学术期刊义在十八世纪占据主导。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the journal stem; the near-meaning group holds other periodicals and records.
note.cn: 形近组共用 journal 词干；近义组收其他刊物与记录。

entries.definition: A person who writes for newspapers or broadcast.
entries.definitionCN: 由 journal 加 -ist 构成，指新闻工作者。

entries.definition: The work or study of news reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「新闻业；新闻学」。

entries.definition: A trip from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，义为「旅程」，源自同一拉丁「日」词根但路线不同。

entries.definition: A magazine published at regular intervals.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指定期刊物。

entries.definition: A book of daily personal notes.
entries.definitionCN: 指个人的日记本，更私人。

entries.definition: An official record of events.
entries.definitionCN: 技术上指正式运行记录。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from Latin dies, a day, to the library shelf of bound volumes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「日」走到图书馆那排合订本。

normal.en: The root is dies, day, also seen in diary and diurnal.
normal.cn: 词根是 dies「日」，也见于 diary 与 diurnal。

normal.en: Journalist adds -ist to the periodical noun.
normal.cn: journalist 是给期刊名词加 -ist。

normal.en: Keep a journal is the personal use, at home.
normal.cn: keep a journal 是家里的私人用法。

normal.en: An academic journal is the professional use.
normal.cn: academic journal 是专业领域的用法。

normal.en: Jour and dies both survive in French and Latin day words.
normal.cn: 法语 jour 与拉丁 dies 都是「日」的词。

abstract.en: A journal is a day pressed flat into pages.
abstract.cn: 期刊就是把一天压平成纸页。

abstract.en: The same word holds a scholar and a schoolgirl.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既装着学者也装着女学生。

abstract.en: Bound volumes are years standing on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 合订本就是站在书架上的一整年。

examples.en: The journal publishes four issues a year.
examples.cn: 这本期刊一年出四期。

examples.en: He writes in his journal before sleep.
examples.cn: 他睡前写日志。

examples.en: Her article appeared in an academic journal.
examples.cn: 她的文章登在一份学术期刊上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「 jour 日」加「nal」—— 每天一页，就是日志

root: 拉丁语 dies「日」→ diurnus「白日的」→ diurnalis → 古法语 journal「每日的；日志」→ 英语 journal。同族 diary、journalist、journey。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: a specialist periodical, a daily paper, a personal diary, a log, a society volume, and a travel account.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：专业期刊、日报、个人日记、运行日志、学会汇编，以及旅行游记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pages bound by dates, one day after another.
core.cn: 核心意象：按日期订起来的纸页，一天接一天。

branches.en: THE LIBRARY SHELF: issues bound into yearly volumes.
branches.cn: 书架这条线：各期合订成年卷。

branches.en: THE NEWS STAND: a paper that comes every morning.
branches.cn: 报摊这条线：每天早上来的报纸。

branches.en: THE DESK DRAWER: a private day book and a travel tale.
branches.cn: 抽屉这条线：私人的日记与行旅记述。

branches.en: THE ENGINE ROOM: an official log of faults.
branches.cn: 轮机舱这条线：正式记录的故障。

branches.en: THE PEER REVIEW: the gate where research is published.
branches.cn: 同行评议这条线：研究发表的关口。

intro.en: Journal carries the Latin day root di- and takes English endings for its family.
intro.cn: journal 带着拉丁「日」词根 di-，词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives come from dies, a day, through diurnalis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词经由 diurnalis 来自 dies「日」。

definition_zh: 判断；意见；审判；裁决；判断力
definition_en: an opinion you form about something, or a decision given by a court or an authority
core_image: 天平两端落定，指针停住不再摆动
scene: 会议结束时，大家等着主持人给个说法。Her judgement on the matter was accepted by everyone at the table.
sceneCN: 这里 judgement 是「判断、意见」（第 1 个义项：对某事形成的看法），句意为她对这件事的判断被在座所有人接受。画面里的物件：会议桌、文件、水杯。

pos.zh: 名词：判断；意见；审判；裁决；判断力

derivatives.zh: 基础词，指法官或评判者
基础动词义，指评判、判断
由 judgement 加 -al 构成，义为「爱评判人的」
加前缀 mis- 构成，义为「判断失误」

senses.title: An opinion formed about something
senses.definition: a considered opinion or conclusion about a situation, person, or plan
senses.definitionCN: 对情形、人或计划经过考虑后形成的看法或结论
senses.example: In my judgement the plan will cost too much.
senses.exampleCN: 依我看，这个计划花费太大。
senses.why: Judging is the act of weighing, and judgement is the scale coming to rest.
senses.whyCN: 评判是称量的动作，judgement 就是秤停下来时的结果。

senses.title: A decision of a court
senses.definition: a formal decision given by a court or judge
senses.definitionCN: 法院或法官作出的正式裁决
senses.example: The court will give its judgement next month.
senses.exampleCN: 法院下个月作出判决。
senses.why: The legal sense fixes the moment when weighing becomes binding.
senses.whyCN: 法律义把「称量」变成「必须执行的时刻」固定下来。

senses.title: The ability to judge well
senses.definition: the ability to make sensible decisions, especially in difficult situations
senses.definitionCN: 作出合理决定的能力，尤指在困难情形中
senses.example: She showed good judgement in a crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 她在危机中表现出很好的判断力。
senses.why: Ability grows out of repeated acts: the noun comes to name the power behind them.
senses.whyCN: 能力来自反复的评判行为，名词于是用来指这些行为背后的力量。

senses.title: A divine or final verdict
senses.definition: a verdict believed to come from a higher power, or a final decision beyond appeal
senses.definitionCN: 被视为来自更高力量的裁决，或无法再上诉的终审
senses.example: The old tale speaks of a day of judgement.
senses.exampleCN: 那个古老的故事讲到审判之日。
senses.why: A verdict thought to be final is the oldest and heaviest layer of the word.
senses.whyCN: 被看作最终的裁决，是这个词最古老也最沉重的一层。

senses.title: A critical assessment in work
senses.definition: an assessment given by an expert, as in a competition or review
senses.definitionCN: 专家在比赛或评审中给出的评估结论
senses.example: The panel's judgement favoured the second design.
senses.exampleCN: 评审团的评估倾向于第二个设计。
senses.why: Expert weighing is the professional face of the same scale, applied to plans.
senses.whyCN: 专家的称量是同一杆秤的专业面孔，只是用来称方案。

senses.title: The act of forming an opinion
senses.definition: the mental process of comparing and deciding rather than the result
senses.definitionCN: 指比较与决定的思维过程，而不是结果本身
senses.example: Clear criteria make judgement easier.
senses.exampleCN: 清晰的准则让评判更容易。
senses.why: Naming the process rather than the result keeps the action side of -ment alive.
senses.whyCN: 指过程而不指结果，让 -ment 里「行为」那一面保留下来。

intro.en: Judgement is judge plus the French-derived noun ending -ment; judge itself comes from Latin judex through French.
intro.cn: judgement 是 judge 加源自法语的 -ment 名词词尾；judge 本身经由法语来自拉丁语 judex。

items.en: judex combined jus, law, and dicere, to say, meaning one who says the law.
items.cn: judex 由 jus「法」和 dicere「说」合成，指宣说法律的人。

items.en: Old French juge named a judge or a court officer.
items.cn: 古法语 juge 指法官或法庭官员。

items.en: English took judge in the thirteenth century and added -ment for the result.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 judge，并加 -ment 表示结果。

items.en: The noun ending -ment came from French and marks an act or its outcome.
items.cn: 名词词尾 -ment 来自法语，表示行为或其结果。

items.en: British English kept judgement while American practice prefers judgment.
items.cn: 英式保留 judgement，美式更常用 judgment。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the judge stem; the near-meaning group holds words for decisions and opinions.
note.cn: 形近组共用 judge 词干；近义组收表示裁决与意见的词。

entries.definition: A person who decides, or to form an opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 同源基础词，指法官，也指评判。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the same noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的美式拼写。

entries.definition: The court system and its work.
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，指司法体系。

entries.definition: The decision of a jury in a case.
entries.definitionCN: 法律用语，指陪审团的裁决。

entries.definition: A personal view that may not be final.
entries.definitionCN: 指个人看法，不必是定论。

entries.definition: A careful evaluation of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指经过仔细评估得出的结论。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from jus plus dicere, law and say, to a scale that stops moving.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从 jus 加 dicere「法与说」走到停下来的那杆秤。

normal.en: Judge joins jus, law, and dicere, to say.
normal.cn: judge 由 jus「法」与 dicere「说」合成。

normal.en: The -ment ending marks the result of an action.
normal.cn: -ment 词尾标记行为的结果。

normal.en: In my judgement is the everyday opinion phrase.
normal.cn: in my judgement 是日常表达意见的说法。

normal.en: A court judgement is written and binding.
normal.cn: court judgement 是书面而具约束力的。

normal.en: British keeps judgement, American prefers judgment.
normal.cn: 英式保留 judgement，美式更常用 judgment。

abstract.en: Judgement is a scale that has stopped swaying.
abstract.cn: 判断是停止摆动的那杆秤。

abstract.en: Half the word is law and half is speech.
abstract.cn: 这个词一半是法律，一半是说话。

abstract.en: Good judgement is a stored supply of quiet decisions.
abstract.cn: 好的判断力是积攒起来的安静决定。

examples.en: In my judgement the delay was avoidable.
examples.cn: 依我看，这次延误本可避免。

examples.en: The court delivered its judgement in a single day.
examples.cn: 法院一天之内就作出了判决。

examples.en: He trusted her judgement more than his own.
examples.cn: 比起自己，他更信任她的判断。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎之门特」—— 法官一锤扎下去，判定了

root: 拉丁语 jus「法」+ dicere「说」→ judex「宣法者」→ 古法语 juge → 英语 judge → 加 -ment 构成 judgement。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: a considered opinion, a court decision, the ability to judge, a final verdict, an expert assessment, and the process itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：经考虑的意见、法院判决、判断力、终审裁决、专家评估，以及评判的过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale that sways and finally comes to rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杆摇晃的天平终于停住。

branches.en: THE MEETING ROOM: a view offered and accepted.
branches.cn: 会议室这条线：提出并被接受的一种看法。

branches.en: THE COURT: a written decision with force.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：一份有强制力的书面决定。

branches.en: THE CRISIS: the ability to choose well under pressure.
branches.cn: 危机这条线：压力下做出好选择的能力。

branches.en: THE LAST DAY: a verdict no one can appeal.
branches.cn: 最后一日这条线：无人能再上诉的裁决。

branches.en: THE PANEL: comparing plans and writing the result.
branches.cn: 评审团这条线：比较方案并写下结果。

intro.en: Judgement is judge plus -ment; the Latin pieces underneath are jus and dicere.
intro.cn: judgement 是 judge 加 -ment，底下是 jus 与 dicere 两块拉丁材料。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives come from judex and judicare, from jus and dicere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词来自 judex 与 judicare，由 jus 和 dicere 组成。

definition_zh: 年少的；初级的；资历较浅的；下级的；职位低的；较年轻者
definition_en: younger in age, or lower in rank or experience than someone else
core_image: 队列里排在后面、个子还矮一头的那个新人
scene: 办公室里最新的那个人坐在靠门的位置，桌上只摆着一台旧电脑。As a junior clerk, he handled the files nobody else wanted.
sceneCN: 这里 junior 是「初级的、资历浅的」（第 1 个义项：在职位或经验上低于他人），句意为作为初级职员，他处理没人愿意管的档案。画面里的物件：办公室、靠门的桌子、旧电脑。

pos.zh: 形容词：年少的；初级的；资历浅的；下级的
名词：较年轻者；下级；初级职员

derivatives.zh: 由 junior 加 -ity 构成，义为「资历较浅的状态」
由 junior 加 -ate 构成，指修会培养期或初级阶段

senses.title: Lower in rank or experience
senses.definition: having a lower position or less experience than others in the same organization
senses.definitionCN: 在同一机构中职位较低或经验较少
senses.example: She started as a junior designer in the studio.
senses.exampleCN: 她在工作室从初级设计师做起。
senses.why: Rank is the comparison that matters most in offices, staff against staff.
senses.whyCN: 在办公室里最重要的比较是职位，是员工与员工之间的比较。

senses.title: Younger in age
senses.definition: younger than another person, often used of a son named after his father
senses.definitionCN: 年龄小于他人，常用于父子同名的场合
senses.example: He is three years junior to his brother.
senses.exampleCN: 他比哥哥小三岁。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply younger, and it still keeps the Latin comparison.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的一层意思就是「更年轻」，它仍保留着拉丁语比较级的底子。

senses.title: Of the lower school level
senses.definition: relating to the earlier part of a school or a college year
senses.definitionCN: 指学校的低年级阶段或大学三年级
senses.example: She teaches at a junior school near the park.
senses.exampleCN: 她在公园附近的一所小学教书。
senses.why: Schools borrow the age comparison and turn it into a stage of study.
senses.whyCN: 学校借用了年龄比较，把它变成一个学段。

senses.title: A person of lower rank
senses.definition: a person who holds a lower position than someone else
senses.definitionCN: 职位低于他人的人
senses.example: The partners rarely listen to the juniors.
senses.exampleCN: 合伙人很少听下属的意见。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a person: the lower-ranked member of the team.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成一个人：团队中位次较低的那个成员。

senses.title: Smaller in a competition class
senses.definition: belonging to a younger age group in sport or contests
senses.definitionCN: 指体育或竞赛中属于较年轻年龄组
senses.example: He won the junior title at fifteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他十五岁就拿下了少年组冠军。
senses.why: Sport turns age into a class, with its own titles and records.
senses.whyCN: 体育把年龄变成一个组别，有自己的冠军和纪录。

senses.title: The third college year
senses.definition: in American usage, the third year of a four-year course
senses.definitionCN: 美式用法中指四年制课程的第三年
senses.example: She spent her junior year abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她大三那年去了国外。
senses.why: In a four-year course the third year is junior to the last one.
senses.whyCN: 在四年制课程里，第三年比上年一级「低」，于是叫 junior year。

intro.en: Junior was borrowed from Latin junior, the comparative of juvenis, young; English uses it unchanged.
intro.cn: junior 直接借自拉丁语 junior，是 juvenis「年轻」的比较级；英语原样沿用。

items.en: juvenis meant young, and junior was its comparative form.
items.cn: juvenis 意为年轻的，junior 是它的比较级。

items.en: The -or ending marks the comparative, as in senior.
items.cn: -or 词尾标记比较级，senior 也是如此。

items.en: English borrowed junior in the sixteenth century as an adjective and noun.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 junior，兼作形容词和名词。

items.en: The rank sense spread through offices and armed forces.
items.cn: 「职位较低」这一义在机关和军队中扩散。

items.en: The school senses, junior school and junior year, settled in the modern period.
items.cn: 初级学校与大学三年级等教育义在近现代固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds Latin comparatives that end in -or; the near-meaning group holds words for younger and lower rank.
note.cn: 形近组收以 -or 结尾的拉丁比较级；近义组收表示年幼与低级的词。

entries.definition: Older or higher in rank.
entries.definitionCN: junior 的反义对应词，义为「年长的；高级的」。

entries.definition: Young, or a young person.
entries.definitionCN: 同源于 juvenis，义为「少年的」。

entries.definition: The state of being junior.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，指资历较浅的状态。

entries.definition: Less old than another person.
entries.definitionCN: 最简单直白的「更年轻的」。

entries.definition: Lower in rank within a system.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指体制中下级。

entries.definition: Someone being trained for a job.
entries.definitionCN: 指正在受训的岗位新人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the Latin comparative ending to the desk by the door.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语比较级词尾走到靠门的那张桌子。

normal.en: Junior is the comparative of juvenis, young.
normal.cn: junior 是 juvenis「年轻」的比较级。

normal.en: The pair junior and senior is fixed in offices and schools.
normal.cn: junior 与 senior 这一对在机关和学校都固定。

normal.en: Junior to someone uses to, not than.
normal.cn: junior to someone 用 to，不用 than。

normal.en: Junior high school covers the early teenage years.
normal.cn: junior high school 指初中阶段。

normal.en: In American colleges junior year is the third year.
normal.cn: 美国大学的 junior year 是第三年。

abstract.en: A junior is one row back in the same line.
abstract.cn: 初级者是在同一条队伍里后退一排的人。

abstract.en: The word is a comparison, so it always needs another person.
abstract.cn: 这个词是比较，因此总需要另一个人才成立。

abstract.en: Everyone is junior to someone, and senior to someone else.
abstract.cn: 每个人对某些人初级，对另一些人高级。

examples.en: Two junior staff members handled the whole report.
examples.cn: 两名初级员工完成了整份报告。

examples.en: My sister is junior to me by two years.
examples.cn: 我妹妹比我小两岁。

examples.en: He is looking for a junior position in design.
examples.cn: 他在找一个设计方面的初级职位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「就是你儿」—— 家里年纪最小的那个，就是初级选手

root: 拉丁语 juvenis「年轻的」→ 比较级 junior → 英语 junior，原样借用；同族的反义比较级是 senior。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: lower rank, younger age, lower school level, a lower-ranked person, a younger contest class, and the third college year.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：职位较低、年纪较小、学校初段、下级人员、少年组，以及大学三年级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person standing a row behind and half a head lower.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在后退一排、矮半头的位置。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a new desk and the files nobody wants.
branches.cn: 办公室这条线：新桌子与没人要的档案。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: the son who shares the father's name.
branches.cn: 家庭这条线：与父亲同名的儿子。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: early years and the third college year.
branches.cn: 学校这条线：低年级与大学三年级。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the younger age bracket of a contest.
branches.cn: 赛场这条线：比赛的较年轻年龄组。

branches.en: THE LADDER: every rung is junior to the one above.
branches.cn: 梯子这条线：每一级都低于它上面那一级。

intro.en: Junior is a Latin comparative borrowed whole; English adds only a few endings.
intro.cn: junior 是整体借来的拉丁比较级，英语只添了少数词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives all grow from juvenis, young.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词都从 juvenis「年轻」长出来。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 junior 与 senior。

items.example: More junior is the periphrastic form.
items.exampleCN: more junior 是分析式比较级。

definition_zh: 陪审团；评判委员会；评奖团
definition_en: a group of ordinary people chosen to listen to a case and decide it, or a group that decides a competition
core_image: 十二个人坐在木栏后面，低头听完双方发言再做结论
scene: 法庭里空气很闷，旁听席坐满了人，栏杆后那一组人一直在记笔记。The jury returned after four hours with a clear verdict.
sceneCN: 这里 jury 是「陪审团」（第 1 个义项：依法听审并裁决的一组普通公民），句意为陪审团四小时后回来，给出了明确的裁决。画面里的物件：法庭、木栏、笔记本。

pos.zh: 名词：陪审团；评判委员会；评奖团（集合用法）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 jur- 加 -or 构成，指陪审员
由 jur- 加 -ist 构成，指法学家
由 jur- 加 -idical 构成，义为「司法上的」
由 jur- 加 dictio 构成，义为「司法管辖权」

senses.title: A body deciding a court case
senses.definition: a group of citizens sworn to hear evidence and give a verdict in a court
senses.definitionCN: 依法宣誓听取证据并在法庭上作出裁决的一组公民
senses.example: The jury took two days to reach a verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 陪审团用了两天得出结论。
senses.why: The core sense is a sworn body that speaks a verdict for the court.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是向法庭宣告裁决的一个宣誓团体。

senses.title: A panel judging a competition
senses.definition: a group of people chosen to judge a contest and choose winners
senses.definitionCN: 被选出为一比评优劣、决定获奖者的一组人
senses.example: The jury gave the prize to an unknown filmmaker.
senses.exampleCN: 评委会把奖给了一位无名导演。
senses.why: A contest panel judges the way a court does: it weighs and decides.
senses.whyCN: 比赛的评委与法庭一样评判：称量然后决定。

senses.title: Members collectively, with plural agreement
senses.definition: the group treated as a plural body in grammar, so the jury can be said to disagree
senses.definitionCN: 语法上按复数处理，因此可说陪审团意见不一致
senses.example: The jury were still arguing at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 到九点陪审团还在争论。
senses.why: British grammar lets a collective noun take a plural verb when the members act apart.
senses.whyCN: 英式语法允许集合名词在成员各自行动时接复数动词。

senses.title: A temporary makeshift device
senses.definition: a temporary arrangement in nautical or technical use, as a makeshift mast
senses.definitionCN: 航海或技术语境中的临时凑合装置，如临时桅杆
senses.example: They rigged a jury rudder after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后他们装了一副临时舵。
senses.why: Sailors use the word for a thing thrown together to meet an emergency.
senses.whyCN: 水手用这个词指为应付紧急情况匆匆凑成的东西。

senses.title: A body of citizens summoned by law
senses.definition: the body of citizens summoned to serve, seen as an institution
senses.definitionCN: 被依法召集服役的公民群体，作为制度看待
senses.example: Jury service is a duty of the citizen.
senses.exampleCN: 担任陪审员是公民的义务。
senses.why: The institution side names not a case but the standing role of citizens in law.
senses.whyCN: 制度这一面指的不是某个案子，而是公民在法律中的常设角色。

intro.en: Jury comes from Old French juree, an oath, from Latin jurare, to swear, and shares the root jus, law.
intro.cn: jury 来自古法语 juree「誓言」，源自拉丁语 jurare「宣誓」，与 jus「法」同根。

items.en: jurare meant to swear an oath, and jus meant law or right.
items.cn: jurare 意为宣誓，jus 意为法或权利。

items.en: juree named a sworn body of men or the oath they took.
items.cn: juree 指宣誓组成的一群人，或他们所立的誓言。

items.en: English borrowed jury in the fourteenth century as the sworn body in a court.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 jury，指法庭上的宣誓团体。

items.en: The competition sense developed much later, as prizes became contests.
items.cn: 比赛评委义很晚才出现，源于评奖变成竞赛。

items.en: The nautical jury sense is separate and probably from a different source.
items.cn: 航海上的 jury 义是另一回事，很可能来源不同。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin jur- root of law; the near-meaning group holds related bodies and legal roles.
note.cn: 形近组共用拉丁「法」词根 jur-；近义组收相关机构与法律角色。

entries.definition: A member of a jury.
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，指陪审员。

entries.definition: An expert in law.
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，指法学家。

entries.definition: The authority of a court over a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，指司法管辖权。

entries.definition: The decision a jury gives.
entries.definitionCN: 指陪审团作出的裁决。

entries.definition: A small group chosen to advise or judge.
entries.definitionCN: 指被选出评审或咨询的小组。

entries.definition: A body appointed to judge a special matter.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指审理专门事项的裁判机构。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the group to swearing an oath and to the contest panel.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个团体连到宣誓，也连到比赛的评委会。

normal.en: Latin jurare, to swear, is the parent of jury.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jurare「宣誓」是 jury 的亲本。

normal.en: Juror adds -or to the Latin root jur-.
normal.cn: juror 在拉丁词根 jur- 后加 -or。

normal.en: Jury is a collective noun, so a jury can be singular or plural in agreement.
normal.cn: jury 是集合名词，主谓一致可单可复。

normal.en: Grand jury is the American term for a group that decides charges.
normal.cn: grand jury 是美国指决定是否起诉的团体。

normal.en: Jury also judges cakes and films at festivals.
normal.cn: jury 在电影节和比赛里也评判作品。

abstract.en: A jury is twelve ordinary chairs pulled together to decide.
abstract.cn: 陪审团是十二把普通椅子凑在一起做决定。

abstract.en: They swear first and speak after.
abstract.cn: 他们先宣誓，后开口。

abstract.en: A group is trusted where a single voice might lean.
abstract.cn: 一个人可能偏，于是一群人被信任。

examples.en: The jury cleared him of all charges.
examples.cn: 陪审团洗清了他的全部指控。

examples.en: She was called for jury service in March.
examples.cn: 她三月被通知担任陪审员。

examples.en: A jury of five chose the winning film.
examples.cn: 由五人组成的评委会选出了获奖影片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「主意」—— 十几个人一起拿主意，就是陪审团

root: 拉丁语 jus「法」、jurare「宣誓」→ 古法语 juree「誓言；宣誓的一群人」→ 英语 jury。同族 juror、jurist、jurisdiction。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: a sworn court body, a contest panel, its plural agreement, a nautical makeshift, and the institution of summoned citizens.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：法庭陪审团、比赛评委会、复数一致的用法、航海临时装置，以及被召集公民的制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group of ordinary people who swear and then decide.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群普通人先宣誓，再作决定。

branches.en: THE COURTROOM: evidence heard from both sides.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：听取双方的证据。

branches.en: THE FESTIVAL: films watched and ranked.
branches.cn: 影展这条线：看片并排序。

branches.en: THE LATE ROOM: a group that has not agreed yet.
branches.cn: 深夜评议室这条线：还没取得一致的团体。

branches.en: THE STORM: a rudder lashed together in a hurry.
branches.cn: 风暴这条线：匆匆捆出的临时舵。

branches.en: THE SUMMONS: a letter that makes service a duty.
branches.cn: 传票这条线：一封信把服役变成义务。

intro.en: Jury is borrowed from French and shares the Latin law root jur- with many other words.
intro.cn: jury 从法语借来，与其他许多词共用拉丁「法」词根 jur-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives come from jus and jurare, law and to swear.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词来自 jus 与 jurare，即「法」与「宣誓」。

items.example: The word keeps the oath sense.

definition_zh: 正好；仅仅；刚刚；只是；公正的；恰好的
definition_en: exactly at that point, only a moment ago, merely, or fair and right
core_image: 一根线刚好对齐刻度，不多一分也不少一分
scene: 两个人在门口互相看了一眼，谁都没说话。He was just leaving when the phone rang.
sceneCN: 这里 just 是「刚要」（第 1 个义项：正好处在某个时点上），句意为他正要出门时电话响了。画面里的物件：门口、外套、响起的电话。

pos.zh: 副词：正好；刚刚；仅仅；只是；简直
形容词：公正的；正当的；恰当的

derivatives.zh: 由 just 加 -ice 构成，义为「正义；司法」
由 just 加 -ly 构成，义为「公正地」
由 just 加 -ify 构成，义为「证明正当」
加前缀 un- 构成，义为「不公正的」

senses.title: Exactly at a point in time or space
senses.definition: exactly at a particular moment, or exactly at a place or amount
senses.definitionCN: 恰好在某一时刻，或恰好是某处、某个量
senses.example: The train arrived just as we reached the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 我们刚到闸口，火车就到了。
senses.why: The oldest core is exactness: neither earlier nor later, neither more nor less.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的核心是「恰好」：不早不晚，不多不少。

senses.title: A very short time ago
senses.definition: a very short time ago, in the immediate past
senses.definitionCN: 刚刚过去的一小段时间
senses.example: She has just called from the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她刚从车站打来电话。
senses.why: A point so close to now that it barely qualifies as past.
senses.whyCN: 一个离现在极近的时刻，勉强算作过去。

senses.title: Only or merely
senses.definition: no more than the stated amount or thing
senses.definitionCN: 不超过所说的数量或事物
senses.example: It was just a small mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是个小错误。
senses.why: Exactness narrows to a single item, leaving everything else outside.
senses.whyCN: 「恰好」收窄到只有一个，其他都被排除在外。

senses.title: Fair according to what is right
senses.definition: acting or given in accordance with what is right and deserved
senses.definitionCN: 依照正当标准行事或给予的
senses.example: A just settlement was reached within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一周内达成了公正的解决方案。
senses.why: The adjective sense moves from exact measure to fair measure: what is deserved to a hair.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义从精确的度量走到公平的度量：应得的一丝不差。

senses.title: Barely enough or almost not
senses.definition: only barely, so that the result is almost the opposite
senses.definitionCN: 指仅仅勉强达到，结果几乎相反
senses.example: We just made it before the gate closed.
senses.exampleCN: 我们刚好在关门前进去了。
senses.why: The exactness of just is stretched to its limit: one second more and it fails.
senses.whyCN: 「恰好」被拉到极限：再多一秒就不成了。

senses.title: Used to soften a request or statement
senses.definition: in a request, used to make the tone lighter or politer
senses.definitionCN: 请求中用来让语气更轻或更客气
senses.example: Could you just wait outside for a moment?
senses.exampleCN: 你能在外面稍等一会儿吗？
senses.why: Just here lowers the weight of a request, asking for the smallest possible amount.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 just 减轻了请求的分量，只要求最小的那一点。

intro.en: Just comes from Latin justus, "lawful, right", from jus, law; the same word therefore covers both exactness and fairness.
intro.cn: just 来自拉丁语 justus「合法的、正当的」，源词 jus「法」；因此它同时覆盖「恰好」与「公正」两面。

items.en: jus meant law or right, and justus meant conforming to it.
items.cn: jus 意为法或权利，justus 意为符合法的。

items.en: Old French juste kept the sense of right and exactly fitting.
items.cn: 古法语 juste 保留了「正当」与「恰好合适」两种意思。

items.en: English borrowed just as both adjective and adverb in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪把 just 兼作形容词和副词借入。

items.en: The exactness sense, just right or just now, grew from fitting perfectly.
items.cn: 「恰好」义从「完全契合」发展而来。

items.en: The merely sense developed from the idea of exactly this and no more.
items.cn: 「仅仅」义从「恰好只有这些，不多」发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin jus root; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of time, degree, and fairness.
note.cn: 形近组共用拉丁 jus 词根；近义组收时间、程度与公平类副词。

entries.definition: Fairness, or the legal system.
entries.definitionCN: 同源名词，义为「正义；司法」。

entries.definition: In a fair way.
entries.definitionCN: 由 just 加 -ly 构成，义为「公正地」。

entries.definition: To show that something is right.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「证明正当」。

entries.definition: No more than; merely.
entries.definitionCN: 副词义为「仅仅」，与第 3 个义项最近。

entries.definition: With no difference at all.
entries.definitionCN: 副词义为「恰好」，与第 1 个义项最近。

entries.definition: Treating people equally and rightly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「公平的」，与第 4 个义项最近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from Latin law to the moment before the phone rings.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「法」走到电话响前的那个瞬间。

normal.en: Latin jus, law, is the root of just, justice, and justify.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jus「法」是 just、justice、justify 的共同词根。

normal.en: Just as means at the same instant that something else happens.
normal.cn: just as 表示另一件事正在发生的同一瞬间。

normal.en: Just now means a moment ago, not at this instant.
normal.cn: just now 指刚才，而不是此刻。

normal.en: Just a moment is the polite way to ask for a short wait.
normal.cn: just a moment 是请人稍等的客气说法。

normal.en: The adjective just is rare in speech but regular in law and argument.
normal.cn: 形容词 just 口语少用，但在法律和论证里很常见。

abstract.en: Just is a line laid exactly on a mark.
abstract.cn: just 就是把线正压在刻度上。

abstract.en: The same word measures time and measures fairness.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既量时间，也量公平。

abstract.en: Exactness and justice are both a matter of not tipping the scale.
abstract.cn: 精确与公正，都是不让秤歪。

examples.en: The phone rang just as I sat down.
examples.cn: 我刚坐下电话就响了。

examples.en: He has just finished the last page.
examples.cn: 他刚刚看完最后一页。

examples.en: It was just a joke, nothing more.
examples.cn: 那只是个玩笑，没别的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎死特」—— 分寸掐得正正好，分毫不差

root: 拉丁语 jus「法、权利」→ justus「合法的、正当的」→ 古法语 juste → 英语 just；同族 justice、justify、justly。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: exactness in time, the immediate past, mere amount, fairness, bare sufficiency, and a softening request.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：时间或位置的恰好、刚刚过去、仅仅、公正、勉强够，以及缓和语气的「稍」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line set exactly on the mark, no slip either way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根线正压在刻度上，两边都不偏。

branches.en: THE PLATFORM: the train meets the moment you arrive.
branches.cn: 站台这条线：火车正好在你到时进站。

branches.en: THE PHONE: a call from a minute ago.
branches.cn: 电话这条线：一分钟前打来的。

branches.en: THE SMALL WORD: merely, and a gentle please wait.
branches.cn: 小小的语气词：仅仅，以及客气地请人稍等。

branches.en: THE SCALES: what someone deserves, to a hair.
branches.cn: 天平这条线：一个人应得的分毫不差。

branches.en: THE CLOSING GATE: through by a centimetre.
branches.cn: 关门这条线：差一厘米就进不来。

intro.en: Just is the bare Latin adjective; its family takes Latin and English endings.
intro.cn: just 是裸露的拉丁形容词，它的词族要加拉丁或英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives descend from jus, law, and justus, lawful.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词源自 jus「法」与 justus「合法的」。

definition_zh: 正义；公正；公平；司法；审判；法官（头衔）
definition_en: the quality of being fair and right, or the system that courts use to decide what is right
core_image: 蒙眼的女像一手持天平，一手持剑，稳稳立在台阶之上
scene: 法院门口的台阶上，两排石柱之间刻着一句关于公平的铭文。The family is still waiting for justice after ten years.
sceneCN: 这里 justice 是「公正、正义」（第 1 个义项：公平正当的品质），句意为十年过去，这家人仍在等待公正。画面里的物件：法院、台阶、石刻铭文。

pos.zh: 名词：正义；公正；司法；审判；（法官头衔）大法官

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「公正的」
由 just 加 -ly 构成，义为「公正地」
同源动词，义为「证明正当」
加前缀 in- 构成，义为「不公正」
由 justice 派生，指司法官或司法机构

senses.title: Fairness as a quality
senses.definition: the quality of being fair and giving each person what is due
senses.definitionCN: 公平待人、各得其所的品质
senses.example: She fought for justice for the workers.
senses.exampleCN: 她为工人们争取公正。
senses.why: The core is fairness treated as a thing worth having and defending.
senses.whyCN: 核心是被当作值得争取与守护之物的公平。

senses.title: The system of courts
senses.definition: the legal system and the process of judging cases
senses.definitionCN: 法律体系以及审理案件的程序
senses.example: The case will go through the criminal justice system.
senses.exampleCN: 此案将走刑事司法程序。
senses.why: Fairness put into institutions becomes a system of courts and procedure.
senses.whyCN: 公平被装进机构，就变成法院与程序构成的体系。

senses.title: A fair outcome for someone
senses.definition: the fair result that a person has been denied or is owed
senses.definitionCN: 被剥夺或应得的那份公平结果
senses.example: The families finally got justice in court.
senses.exampleCN: 这些家庭终于在法庭上得到了公正。
senses.why: Here the abstract quality turns into a concrete settlement someone receives.
senses.whyCN: 这里抽象的品质变成某人实际得到的结果。

senses.title: A title for a judge
senses.definition: a formal title for a judge of a high court
senses.definitionCN: 高等法院法官的正式头衔
senses.example: Justice Hill wrote the opinion for the court.
senses.exampleCN: 希尔大法官为法庭撰写了意见。
senses.why: A person who embodies fairness in court takes the abstract noun as a title.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上代表公平的人，直接拿了那个抽象名词当头衔。

senses.title: Fair treatment in presentation
senses.definition: the quality of doing full justice to a subject or a person
senses.definitionCN: 指充分、恰当呈现某题材或某人的水准
senses.example: The film does justice to a difficult story.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影充分展现了那个难讲的故事。
senses.why: Giving a subject its due is the same fairness applied to description.
senses.whyCN: 把题材应得的分量给它，是公平用在了描写上。

senses.title: Rightness in judgement
senses.definition: the correctness of a decision or evaluation
senses.definitionCN: 指决定或评价的正确恰当
senses.example: There is some justice in his complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 他的抱怨有几分道理。
senses.why: A verdict that measures correctly is justice in miniature.
senses.whyCN: 量得准确的一次判断，就是缩小的正义。

intro.en: Justice comes from Latin justitia, fairness, from justus, lawful, and jus, law, through Old French.
intro.cn: justice 来自拉丁语 justitia「公平」，源自 justus「合法的」与 jus「法」，经由古法语进入英语。

items.en: justitia named the quality of being just, and justus came from jus, law.
items.cn: justitia 指「公正的品质」，justus 源自 jus「法」。

items.en: Old French justise carried both fairness and the right to judge.
items.cn: 古法语 justise 同时带着公平与审判权两层意思。

items.en: English took justice in the twelfth century for fairness and the courts.
items.cn: 英语在十二世纪借入 justice，指公平与法庭。

items.en: The title Justice for a high court judge settled in later use.
items.cn: 作为高院法官头衔的 Justice 在后世固定下来。

items.en: The phrase do justice to extended it to art and description.
items.cn: do justice to 这一说法把它延伸到艺术与描写。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin law root; the near-meaning group holds other words for fairness and law.
note.cn: 形近组共用拉丁「法」词根；近义组收其他表示公平与法律的词。

entries.definition: Fair, or exactly.
entries.definitionCN: 同源基础词，义为「公正的」或「正好」。

entries.definition: To give good reasons for something.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「证明正当」。

entries.definition: Unfair treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 加 in- 构成，义为「不公正」。

entries.definition: The quality of treating people equally.
entries.definitionCN: 最日常的「公平」，语气朴素。

entries.definition: Fairness, especially where equal treatment must be adjusted.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指衡平与实质公平。

entries.definition: The set of rules a society enforces.
entries.definitionCN: 指社会强制执行的法律规则本身。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from Latin jus to the steps of a courthouse.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语 jus「法」走到法院门前的台阶。

normal.en: The root jus, law, also gives just and justify.
normal.cn: 词根 jus「法」还生出 just 与 justify。

normal.en: Bring someone to justice means get them into court.
normal.cn: bring someone to justice 指把人送上法庭。

normal.en: Do justice to is about showing something fully.
normal.cn: do justice to 指把某物充分表现出来。

normal.en: Justice can mean both the quality and the courts.
normal.cn: justice 既指公正的品质，也指司法机关。

normal.en: Injustice is simply justice with in-.
normal.cn: injustice 就是 justice 加 in-。

abstract.en: Justice is a scale held steady by an unseen hand.
abstract.cn: 正义是一杆被看不见的手扶稳的秤。

abstract.en: The same word is a principle and a building.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既是原则也是一座建筑。

abstract.en: It is fairness given an address and a date.
abstract.cn: 它就是有了地址和日期的公平。

examples.en: They demanded justice for the victims.
examples.cn: 他们为受害者要求公正。

examples.en: The justice system is slow but open.
examples.cn: 司法体系运转缓慢但公开。

examples.en: No photograph can do justice to that valley.
examples.cn: 任何照片都无法展现那条山谷的全部。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎斯蒂斯」—— 秤杆扎稳了，才有正义

root: 拉丁语 jus「法」→ justus「合法的」→ justitia「公正」→ 古法语 justise → 英语 justice；同族 just、justify、injustice。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: fairness as a quality, the court system, a fair outcome, a judge's title, full presentation, and the rightness of a judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：公正的品质、司法体系、应得的公正结果、大法官头衔、充分展现，以及评判得当。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blindfolded figure holding scales and a sword.
core.cn: 核心意象：蒙眼持秤与剑的女像。

branches.en: THE BANNER: a principle that people march for.
branches.cn: 旗帜这条线：人们为之游行的一条原则。

branches.en: THE COURTHOUSE: procedure, lawyers, and hours of waiting.
branches.cn: 法院这条线：程序、律师和漫长的等待。

branches.en: THE VERDICT: a fair result handed to a family.
branches.cn: 裁决这条线：交到家属手里的公正结果。

branches.en: THE BENCH: a title spoken with a name.
branches.cn: 法官席这条线：念出姓氏的头衔。

branches.en: THE PICTURE: a work that shows its subject fully and fairly.
branches.cn: 作品这条线：完整而恰当地表现题材。

intro.en: Justice adds a Latin-derived noun ending to just; the deeper pieces are jus and justus.
intro.cn: justice 给 just 加了一个拉丁来源的名词词尾，更深的部件是 jus 与 justus。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives all descend from jus, law.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词都源自 jus「法」。

items.example: A just ruler weighs both sides.
items.exampleCN: 公正的统治者会称量两边。

definition_zh: 证明……正当；为……辩护；使合理化；调整使排满（排版）
definition_en: to show that something is right or reasonable, or to give a good reason for it
core_image: 有人举起一张纸，一条一条向对面的人解释为什么这样做没错
scene: 会议室里被质问的一方把证据摊开，逐条说明当初的决定为什么合理。Nothing can justify that much expense on one dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 justify 是「证明……正当」（第 1 个义项：给出理由说明某事合理），句意为没有任何理由能为一顿晚饭花那么多钱开脱。画面里的物件：会议室、证据文件、对面的听众。

pos.zh: 动词：证明正当；为……辩解；使合理；（排版）使两端对齐

derivatives.zh: 由 justify 加 -cation 构成，义为「辩护；正当理由」
由 justify 加 -ed 构成，义为「有正当理由的」
由 justify 加 -able 构成，义为「可辩解的」
加前缀 un- 构成，义为「无正当理由的」

senses.title: To show that something is right
senses.definition: to give reasons that show an action or claim is right or reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 给出理由以证明某行为或主张合理
senses.example: How do you justify spending so much on a phone?
senses.exampleCN: 你凭什么为花这么多钱买手机找理由？
senses.why: The word sets a thing on the scale of right and asks whether it balances.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把一件事放上「正当」的秤，问它是否配平。

senses.title: To defend against criticism
senses.definition: to answer criticism by defending a choice or statement
senses.definitionCN: 通过辩护某个选择或说法来回应批评
senses.example: The manager justified his decision to the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 经理向全队为自己的决定作了辩解。
senses.why: Justifying is talking back to an accusation with reasons.
senses.whyCN: 辩解就是用理由回应一项指责。

senses.title: To be a good reason for
senses.definition: to be the reason that makes something acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 本身构成使某事可接受的理由
senses.example: The delay was justified by the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误因暴风雨而有其理由。
senses.why: Here the subject is the reason itself, not the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 这里作主语的是理由本身，而不是说话的人。

senses.title: To set text flush at the margins
senses.definition: in printing, to space text so that both edges line up
senses.definitionCN: 排版中调整字距，使左右两边都对齐
senses.example: The columns are justified so the page looks tidy.
senses.exampleCN: 各栏都两端对齐，页面显得整齐。
senses.why: Typesetting sets lines to exact margins, the same exactness the word always carried.
senses.whyCN: 排版把行对齐到精确的边界，正是这个词一直带有的「精确」。

senses.title: To prove oneself right by result
senses.definition: to be shown right by later events
senses.definitionCN: 指后来的事实说明当初是对的
senses.example: The final score justified the coach's choice.
senses.exampleCN: 最终比分证明了教练的选择。
senses.why: Later facts can do the weighing that argument could not.
senses.whyCN: 后来发生的事实能做论证做不到的那次称量。

senses.title: To declare someone righteous
senses.definition: in theology, to declare a person righteous before God
senses.definitionCN: 神学中指宣告某人在神面前为义
senses.example: The doctrine says faith alone justifies the believer.
senses.exampleCN: 该教义说唯凭信使信徒称义。
senses.why: The theological sense is a declaration of rightness rather than a proof.
senses.whyCN: 神学义是一种宣告其为义，而不是去证明。

intro.en: Justify is Latin justus, right, plus facere, to make: to make right or to show as right.
intro.cn: justify 是拉丁语 justus「正当的」加 facere「做」：使之正当，或显示其为正当。

items.en: justificare meant to make just or to do justice, from justus and facere.
items.cn: justificare 意为使之公正或伸张正义，由 justus 与 facere 组成。

items.en: The -fic- element is a form of facere, to make or do.
